title: TO Thee, Before the Dawning Light
description: TO Thee, Before the Dawning Light in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 2, headed “Secret devotion and spiritual mindedness; or, Constant converse with God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: TO thee, be-fore the daw-ning light, My gra-cious God, I pray; I med-i-tate thy Name by night, And keep thy law by day.

lines: TO thee, before the dawning light,
I meditate thy Name by night,
And keep thy law by day.
My spirit faints to see thy grace,
Seven times a day I lift my hands,
And pay my thanks to thee;
When midnight darkness veils the skies,
I call thy works to mind;
My thoughts in warm devotion rise,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
